findings: Solved 2026-10-29 on the owner's request (Practice, Book exercises): the Chapter 14 exercise as printed (PDF 42-44, printed 39-41) with answers in English and Roman Urdu: 9 MCQs, 8 short answer, 6 constructed response, 6 comprehensive questions and 6 numerical problems. Drafts for the academic review.
The book prints no MCQ key; the keys are worked out from the chapter: 14.1 b, 14.2 b, 14.3 c, 14.4 b, 14.5 c, 14.6 c, 14.7 b, 14.8 d, 14.9 a.

Book correction, numerical 14.4: the printed answers 1.3 s, 3.0 m s-2 and 1.4 m s-1 follow from a mass of 8 kg, not the printed 80 kg. With 80 kg (k = 200 N m-1): T = 3.97 s, a = 0.30 m s-2, v = 0.43 m s-1; the printed K.E. 7.6 J and P.E. 1.44 J are right (independent of the mass).

Numerical 14.1 asks for 'acceleration' and 'velocity' without saying 'maximum'; the printed answers are the maximum values, which are given. Numerical 14.6 follows the book (mgh = 1/2 kx^2, x = 0.2 m); a note adds that counting the extra fall x gives about 0.23 m.

Comprehensive 14.1 and 14.2 use the correct forms T = 2 pi sqrt(m/k) and v = omega sqrt(x0^2 - x^2) where the chapter text misprints them (see the 14.3 and 14.4 lessons). Short 14.2 lists the conditions without the chapter's misprinted 'restoring force proportional to inertia'.

Beyond the chapter: MCQ 14.3 (gravity inside the Earth is proportional to the distance from the centre) and short 14.6 (the Earth's rotation lowers the effective g except at the poles). The Roman Urdu answer to short 14.6 says so in a Wazahat box.
